en.before: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.1.3 requires the organization to define an AI risk treatment process to:
en.after: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.1.3 requires the organization to set out a process for treating AI risk that will:

en.before: - a) **select appropriate AI risk treatment options**, taking account of the risk assessment results;
en.after: - a) **select appropriate AI risk treatment options**, in light of what the risk assessment found;

en.before: - b) **determine all controls that are necessary** to implement the AI risk treatment options chosen, **and compare the controls with those in Annex A** to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted;
en.after: - b) **determine all controls that are necessary** to put the chosen treatment options into effect, **and compare those controls against Annex A** to check that none needed has been left out;

en.before: - c) **consider the controls from Annex A** that are relevant for the implementation of the AI risk treatment options;
en.after: - c) **consider the controls from Annex A** bearing on how the treatment options will be implemented;

en.before: - d) **identify if additional controls are necessary** beyond those in Annex A in order to implement all risk treatment options;
en.after: - d) **identify if additional controls are necessary** past Annex A's, so that every treatment option can be implemented;

en.before: - e) **consider the guidance in Annex B** for the implementation of controls determined in b) and c);
en.after: - e) **consider the guidance in Annex B** when implementing the controls settled at b) and c);

en.before: - f) **produce a statement of applicability** that contains the necessary controls and provides justification for inclusions and exclusions.
en.after: - f) **produce a statement of applicability** listing the necessary controls, with a justification for what is in and what is out.

en.before: Two notes accompany it. NOTE 1 records that Annex A provides reference controls for meeting organizational objectives and addressing risks related to the design and use of AI systems. NOTE 2 records that control objectives and controls are not exhaustive and additional ones can be needed, that the organization can design its own controls or take them from existing sources, and that AI risk management can be integrated in other management systems.
en.after: Two notes accompany it. NOTE 1 records that Annex A offers reference controls for meeting organizational objectives and handling risks that arise from designing and using AI systems. NOTE 2 records that control objectives and controls are not exhaustive and additional ones can be needed, that the organization can design its own controls or take them from existing sources, and that managing AI risk can sit inside other management systems.

en.before: Clause 6.1.3 d) requires the organization to identify if **additional controls are necessary beyond those in Annex A**. NOTE 2 confirms the list is not exhaustive and that the organization can design its own or take them from other sources.
en.after: Clause 6.1.3 d) requires the organization to identify whether **controls beyond Annex A's are necessary**. NOTE 2 confirms the list is not exhaustive and that the organization can design its own or take them from other sources.

en.before: **It records what was decided, not what was done.** A control declared as included and not implemented is a **clause 8.1** finding - the organization shall implement the controls determined according to 6.1.3 that relate to the operation of the AIMS - not a finding against Table A.1 or against the statement of applicability. Lesson 04-12 works this properly.
en.after: **It records what was decided, not what was done.** A control declared as included and not implemented is a **clause 8.1** finding - the organization shall implement those controls settled under 6.1.3 which bear on operating the AIMS - not a finding against Table A.1 or against the statement of applicability. Lesson 04-12 works this properly.

en.before: A note worth carrying: clause 3.26's Note 2 to entry states that all identified risks and the risk management measures established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability. That is a `shall` inside a note to a definition, which is unusual drafting. **Cite clause 6.1.3 f) for the statement of applicability requirement**, not the note - lesson 04-09 covers why a note is not where a finding should rest.
en.after: A note worth carrying: clause 3.26's Note 2 to entry states that all identified risks and the risk management measures established to address them shall appear in the statement of applicability. That is a `shall` inside a note to a definition, which is unusual drafting. **Cite clause 6.1.3 f) for the statement of applicability requirement**, not the note - lesson 04-09 covers why a note is not where a finding should rest.

en.before: The relationship runs one way and through the risk assessment. The NOTE under clause 6.1.2 d) 1) records that when assessing consequences the organization **can utilize an AI system impact assessment as indicated in 6.1.4**. And clause 6.1.4 itself requires the organization to **consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment**.
en.after: The relationship runs one way and through the risk assessment. The NOTE under clause 6.1.2 d) 1) records that when assessing consequences the organization **can draw on an AI system impact assessment, as 6.1.4 indicates**. And clause 6.1.4 itself requires the organization to **take what the AI system impact assessment found into the risk assessment**.

en.before: { "id": "b", "text": "Against clause 8.1, which requires the organization to implement the controls determined according to 6.1.3 that relate to the operation of the AI management system." },
en.after: { "id": "b", "text": "Against clause 8.1, which requires the organization to implement those controls settled under 6.1.3 which bear on operating the AI management system." },

en.before: - The organization **shall define a process for assessing the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies** that can result from the development, provision or use of AI systems.
en.after: - The organization **shall define a process for assessing what may follow for individuals, for groups of them, or both, and for societies** from developing, providing or using AI systems.

en.before: - The AI system impact assessment **shall determine the potential consequences** an AI system's **deployment, intended use and foreseeable misuse** has on individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies.
en.after: - The AI system impact assessment **shall determine the potential consequences** that an AI system's **deployment, intended use and foreseeable misuse** carry for individuals, for groups of them, or both, and for societies.

en.before: - The assessment **shall take into account the specific technical and societal context** where the AI system is deployed **and applicable jurisdictions**.
en.after: - The assessment **shall take account of the specific technical and societal context** of the place the AI system is deployed, **and the jurisdictions that apply**.

en.before: - The **result** of the AI system impact assessment **shall be documented**.
en.after: - The assessment's **result shall be documented**.

en.before: - The organization **shall consider the results** of the AI system impact assessment **in the risk assessment** referred to in 6.1.2.
en.after: - The organization **shall carry the results** of the AI system impact assessment **into the risk assessment** at 6.1.2.

en.before: Where appropriate, the result **can** be made available to relevant interested parties as defined by the organization - a `can`, and the only permissive element in the clause.
en.after: Where appropriate, the result **can** be shared with whichever interested parties the organization names - a `can`, and the only permissive element in the clause.

en.before: Clause 6.1.4's final limb is the hardest to audit and the most valuable when it lands: the organization shall **consider the results** of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment.
en.after: Clause 6.1.4's final limb is the hardest to audit and the most valuable when it lands: the organization shall **carry the results** of the AI system impact assessment into the risk assessment.

en.before: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 7.5.1 requires the organization's AI management system to include:
en.after: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 7.5.1 requires the AI management system to hold:

en.before: - a) **documented information required by this document**;
en.after: - a) **the documented information this document requires**;

en.before: - b) **documented information determined by the organization as being necessary for the effectiveness** of the AI management system.
en.after: - b) **whatever documented information the organization judges necessary** for the AI management system to be effective.

en.before: Clause 7.5.3 requires that documented information be **available and suitable for use where and when it is needed**, and be **adequately protected** - from loss of confidentiality, improper use, or loss of integrity.
en.after: Clause 7.5.3 requires documented information to be **there and fit to use, where and when it is needed**, and to be **adequately protected** - against lost confidentiality, improper use, or lost integrity.

en.before: For its control the organization shall address, as applicable: distribution, access, retrieval and use; storage and preservation, including preservation of legibility; control of changes, such as version control; and retention and disposition. Documented information of external origin determined necessary shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.
en.after: For its control the organization shall address, as applicable: how it is distributed, accessed, retrieved and used; how it is stored and preserved, legibility included; how changes are controlled, such as by version; and how it is retained and disposed of. Documented information of external origin judged necessary shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.

en.before: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 8.1 requires the organization to plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements and to implement the actions determined in Clause 6, by:
en.after: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 8.1 requires the organization to plan, run and control the processes it needs in order to meet requirements and carry out what Clause 6 determined, by:

en.before: - **establishing criteria for the processes**;
en.after: - **setting criteria for those processes**;

en.before: - **implementing control of the processes in accordance with the criteria**.
en.after: - **controlling the processes against those criteria**.

en.before: > The organization **shall implement the controls determined according to 6.1.3** that are related to the operation of the AI management system - for example, AI system development and usage life cycle related controls. **The effectiveness of these controls shall be monitored and corrective actions shall be considered** if the intended results are not achieved.
en.after: > The organization **shall implement the controls settled under 6.1.3** that bear on operating the AI management system - controls tied to the AI system development and usage life cycle, for example. **The effectiveness of those controls shall be monitored, and corrective action shall be considered** where the intended results do not follow.

en.before: And the clause continues with control of changes, review of the consequences of unintended changes, and ensuring that **externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the AI management system are controlled**. Documented information shall be available to the extent necessary to have confidence that processes have been carried out as planned.
en.after: And the clause continues with control of changes, review of the consequences of unintended changes, and ensuring that **externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the AI management system are controlled**. Documented information shall be kept so far as is needed to give confidence that processes ran as planned.

en.before: | AI risk assessment | 6.1.2 | **8.2** - at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur; retain documented information of the results |
en.after: | AI risk assessment | 6.1.2 | **8.2** - at planned intervals, and whenever significant change is proposed or happens; retain documented information of the results |

en.before: **Note the triggers differ slightly between 8.2 and 8.4.** Clause 8.2 says at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur; clause 8.4 says at planned times and when significant changes occur. An auditor testing whether reassessment was triggered should read the clause that applies rather than assume they match.
en.after: **Note the triggers differ slightly between 8.2 and 8.4.** Clause 8.2 says at planned intervals, and whenever significant change is proposed or happens; clause 8.4 says at planned times and when significant changes occur. An auditor testing whether reassessment was triggered should read the clause that applies rather than assume they match.

en.before: Clause 8.1's sentence bears repeating because it is skipped so consistently: **the effectiveness of these controls shall be monitored and corrective actions shall be considered if the intended results are not achieved.**
en.after: Clause 8.1's sentence bears repeating because it is skipped so consistently: **the effectiveness of those controls shall be monitored, and corrective action shall be considered where the intended results do not follow.**

en.before: Clause 8.1 closes with a requirement that is easy to read past: **documented information shall be available to the extent necessary to have confidence that the processes have been carried out as planned.**
en.after: Clause 8.1 closes with a requirement that is easy to read past: **documented information shall be kept so far as is needed to give confidence that the processes ran as planned.**

en.before: Two phrases do work. *To the extent necessary* means the standard is not prescribing volume, which connects to the clause 7.5.1 NOTE and to lesson 04-07's warning against auditing document sets by impression. *Confidence that the processes have been carried out as planned* names the test: could someone establish, from what exists, that the process ran the way it was supposed to?
en.after: Two phrases do work. *To the extent necessary* means the standard is not prescribing volume, which connects to the clause 7.5.1 NOTE and to lesson 04-07's warning against auditing document sets by impression. *Confidence that the processes ran as planned* names the test: could someone establish, from what exists, that the process ran the way it was supposed to?
